subject: Scaling matrix & forecast for renewal — GPU mix and SLO tradeoffs
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia@acme.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal planning: anticipated Q3 usage spike & capacity ask

Hi Alex,

Quick summary from our ops/ML team: post-launch of our new recommendation model (deployed Feb), sustained serving utilization has crept up from 45% to ~78% on our current Dedicated pool during peak windows. We expect a marketing-driven traffic spike in Q3 (projected +65% peak q/q) and want to lock in sizing at renewal so we don't hit throttles.

Key asks:
- Can Redwood propose a suggested GPU mix and minimum tranche for the 12‑month renewal to cover a 3x peak buffer?
- Any options for short-term burst capacity during promotions?
- We'd like a ballpark on incremental monthly cost and whether latency SLOs will be preserved if we add quantized variants.

Attached: acme-usage-q1-2027.csv (hourly tail traces).

Would appreciate a short call this week; Julia + ops-eng@acme.ai are available Thu/Fri morning PST.

Thanks,
Julia Park
Head of ML Ops
Acme Analytics

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Park <julia@acme.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-02T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: anticipated Q3 usage spike & capacity ask

Hi Julia — thanks for the data and heads-up. I ran a quick pass with our capacity heuristics and attached a preliminary "scaling-matrix.xlsx" that maps observed peak TPS to recommended GPU count and model variants. High-level notes:

- For your current traffic shape (78% sustained peak), to hit a 3x promotional buffer we estimate +48 A10G-equivalent GPUs (or ~12 H100s depending on instance sizing).
- We recommend keeping the majority of traffic on an int8/4-bit-quantized variant for cost; keep an fp16 H100 pool as a warm fallback for high-SLO paths.
- Burst options: dedicated reserved burst pool + on-demand fallback (billing at on-demand rate) works well; can convert a percentage of committed capacity to burstable in the contract amend.

I copied Karthik for a technical rundown on latency implications and Marissa for commercial impact / amendment draft. Proposed next steps: internal sizing confirmation -> run a 48hr smoke with a 20% traffic shadow -> finalize amendment.

Available Thu 9:30–11am PST for a quick sync.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Attachments: scaling-matrix.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>, Julia Park <julia@acme.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-07T08:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: anticipated Q3 usage spike & capacity ask

Alex / Julia — digging into the trace and Alex's matrix, a few technical details to call out (quoting Alex below):

> - For your current traffic shape (78% sustained peak), to hit a 3x promotional buffer we estimate +48 A10G-equivalent GPUs (or ~12 H100s depending on instance sizing).
> - We recommend keeping the majority of traffic on an int8/4-bit-quantized variant for cost; keep an fp16 H100 pool as a warm fallback for high-SLO paths.

Analysis:
- Model mix: you have two dominant gen models — RecoLarge (seq 1024, beam-ish serving patterns) and RecoFast (seq 256, low latency). RecoLarge benefits from H100s for throughput; RecoFast is well-suited to A10G / T4 families if quantized.
- KV cache pressure: with RecoLarge the KV cache increases memory pressure; recommend dedicating H100s with 80–90GB RAM per card for those nodes. If you choose a 12‑H100 option, we can shard the large model across 3 GPUs per replica to preserve latency.
- Batching: based on your tail, optimal batch target ~6–10 for RecoLarge during promos; this keeps latency within 120–180ms P95 on H100s. For RecoFast keep batch <=4 to maintain sub-60ms P95 on quantized A10G.
- Autoscale policy: aggressive scale-up (fast) + conservative scale-down (stabilize 5–10m) prevents oscillation during sudden spikes. We should set an ingress threshold that triggers burst-on-demand before commit pool saturates.

Recommendation matrix (short):
- Conservative (min risk): +12 H100s reserved; keep a 16 A10G warm pool for low-latency queries.
- Cost‑balanced: +24 A10G-equivalents + 4 H100s for RecoLarge shards.
- Low-cost (higher risk): +48 A10G-equivalents, quantize aggressively with larger batch windows; expect 10–15% quality delta on RecoLarge.

I'll stand up a quick benchmark job if you confirm which risk profile you prefer. Ben — can you flag any infra constraints for April/May provisioning?

-Karthik
Senior Infra Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>, Julia Park <julia@acme.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-11T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Scaling matrix & forecast for renewal — GPU mix and SLO tradeoffs

Thanks team — pulling commercial threads together. Quick summary & proposed amend: 

- Acme selects the "Cost‑balanced" profile: +24 A10G-equivalents + 4 H100s.
- Contract change: amend committed capacity line item for a 12‑month term, allow up to 20% of commit to be burstable at on-demand rates for two promotional windows (dates TBD).
- Pricing: incremental committed monthly charge = $54,600 (est), on-demand burst rates apply per our standard rate card; I'll attach a renewal-amendment-draft.pdf with numbers.
- Proposed timeline: sign amendment by 2027-05-05 -> provisioning week of 2027-05-12 -> 48hr traffic-shadow in late-May.

Next actions:
1) Julia: confirm approval to proceed with the cost‑balanced sizing by EOD 2027-04-13.
2) Alex/Karthik/Ben: confirm infra availability for provisioning week.
3) I will create the HubSpot amendment and share DocuSign link after confirmation.

Julia — one question on SLOs: if you want strict P95<100ms for RecoFast during promos we should bump the A10G pool by +6 (I called that out in the matrix). Want me to price that alternative?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: renewal-amendment-draft.pdf
Related: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-45291
